queries.api_query: (AFF:"GE HealthCare" OR AFF:"GE Healthcare" OR AFF:"GE Medical Systems" OR AFF:"General Electric Medical Systems") AND (FIRST_PDATE:[2012-01-01 TO 2025-12-31])
(AFF:"Philips" OR AFF:"Philips Healthcare" OR AFF:"Philips Medical Systems") AND (FIRST_PDATE:[2012-01-01 TO 2025-12-31])
(AFF:"Draeger" OR AFF:"Dräger" OR AFF:"Draegerwerk") AND (FIRST_PDATE:[2012-01-01 TO 2025-12-31])

limitations: Query is the frozen FETCH_SPEC.md query executed verbatim (AFF clause AND FIRST_PDATE window). HAS_ABS:Y and SRC:MED were deliberately NOT added: HAS_ABS:Y returns 0 hits for this corpus and SRC:MED would drop preprint (PPR), patent (PAT) and PMC-only records.
Pagination: resultType=core&pageSize=1000, cursorMark; each query stops when nextCursorMark is absent or repeats. reported_hit_count is the hitCount of the first page of that query.

firm_affiliations is a case-insensitive substring test of the frozen firm AFF terms against (a) authorList[].authorAffiliationDetailsList[].authorAffiliation[].affiliation and (b) the record-level affiliation field only. Strings are kept verbatim, de-duplicated, in upstream order. Titles/abstracts are never scanned. Matching normalises whitespace only (upstream uses U+00A0 inside names such as "GE\xa0Healthcare"); retained strings are not altered.
Records returned by more than one firm query: 78 (source_firm is the sorted '+'-joined list). The per-firm retained counts therefore sum to 14069 > records_retained 13980.

Records with empty firm_affiliations: 521 of 13980 - retrieved by the AFF query but no shipped affiliation string matches the firm's own terms; kept in the corpus per spec and counted here rather than silently dropped. All such records are source MED and they are concentrated in 2012-2015. Cause probed on one 2013 example (source MED, id 23295444): the shipped core record carries only unrelated affiliations (a Cape Town hospital), so Europe PMC's AFF index can match an affiliation that is not present in the shipped record; the affiliation data available to the harvester is what is stored, verbatim.

first_publication_date null: 0; date_basis breakdown: {"firstPublicationDate": 13980} (frozen fallback order firstPublicationDate -> electronicPublicationDate -> firstIndexDate -> pubYear + '-01-01'). Upstream date strings are kept verbatim (YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM).
abstract present: 13119 of 13980 (mean collapsed length 1681.49 chars); truncated to 2000 chars: 3811.
source distribution: {"MED": 13661, "PAT": 5, "PMC": 282, "PPR": 32} - no SRC:MED filter was applied, so preprints/patents/PMC-only records are retained.

first_publication_date outside the frozen window despite the server-side FIRST_PDATE filter: 1 record(s), examples ['2005-08-30']. The frozen window is server-side only and no client-side date filter is specified for Europe PMC, so these records are retained and counted. Cause observed: Europe PMC's FIRST_PDATE index is not exactly the shipped firstPublicationDate for every source type (the smoke sample showed a patent record, id WO2006028934, with firstPublicationDate 2005-08-30).

gz verification on write: line count equals records_retained; every line parses as JSON; every record carries exactly the frozen key set; 0 records have abstract_truncated=true with an abstract length != 2000.

Observed hit counts (this run): medtronic reported_hit_count=2892 (returned 2892, retained 2892); ge_healthcare reported_hit_count=4286 (returned 4286, retained 4286); philips reported_hit_count=6615 (returned 6615, retained 6615); draeger reported_hit_count=42 (returned 42, retained 42); mindray reported_hit_count=234 (returned 234, retained 234). After the frozen window is applied, draeger and mindray are far below the informal pre-run estimates (~600 and ~400): AFF:"Draeger" without the window returns 975 records whose top-100 sample is 86% PAT records matching personal surnames (e.g. 'Schumm-Draeger'), inside the frozen window it returns 19, and the frozen three-spelling union returns the value above. The frozen query was not altered to chase the estimate.
AFF:"Philips" also retrieves non-medical Philips (lighting, semiconductors in early years); that contamination is measured later in DATA_INTEGRITY_AUDIT.md, not repaired here.
